name: Shadow & Radius Studio
blurb: layered shadows and radii tuned visually, as one CSS line
intro: Builds a soft, layered box-shadow (several shadows doubling in size, after Josh Comeau's method) and a border-radius, with a live preview you can click to aim the light. Also gives the concentric inner radius for a nested element (outer radius minus padding) and an elevation scale.

inputs.label: Distance
inputs.help: Offset of the largest layer; the elevation.

inputs.label: Spread
inputs.help: Negative tucks the shadow under the box.

inputs.label: Shadow colour
inputs.help: Hex, rgb() or hsl(); tint it with the background hue.

usage: Give distance in px (largest layer offset), direction as a CSS angle in degrees (180 = down), the number of layers (1-8), softness (blur factor), spread in px, total opacity 0-1, the shadow colour (hex, rgb() or hsl()), corner radius and padding in px, and inset true/false. It returns one CSS line with box-shadow and border-radius, the per-layer offsets, blur, spread and alpha, how far the shadow reaches past the box, the nested inner radius, and a 5-step elevation scale of custom properties. Use it to design card, button or modal shadows.
sources: Josh W. Comeau, 'Designing Beautiful Shadows in CSS' (2021) - layered shadows
W3C CSS Backgrounds and Borders Level 3, box-shadow and border-radius
Concentric corners: inner radius = outer radius - padding (rule of thumb)
